text:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Hosted API p99 latency > 12s for 5m. Queue depth: 18,200. Error rate 4.1%. Autoscaler attempted to add GPUs but failures detected. Paging oncall Maya.

maya (oncall): seeing it. pulling up grafana and autoscaler logs. p95 jumped ~600ms -> 3.2s then p99 blew past 12s.

sroder: I can confirm queue backlog on ingress queues, surface-level symptom: GPU pools saturated, autoscaler requests failing with quota responses.

lucas: paste of recent autoscaler log: ```ERROR autoscaler: allocate_gpus failed: QuotaExceeded: requested 8 GPUs, available 4 (region us-west-2). retry_count=3```

maya (oncall): that's consistent with what I see — autoscaler keeps retrying but cloud quota prevents provisioning. current pool sizes: hosted-gpu-prod-a: 32/32 used, hosted-gpu-prod-b: 28/32 used.

nina-prodops: any short-term mitigation we can do besides begging clouds for quota? customers are hitting 504s. support is triaging.

helen-support: multiple customer tickets reporting timeouts for text-generation endpoints; we've labeled severity high for enterprise customers on Dedicated failover. Posting sample ticket: "Generation timed out after 10s, got 504".

sroder: quick plan: 1) reduce long tail work by enabling degraded routing to quantized small models; 2) drop low-priority batch requests; 3) temporarily increase per-tenant rate limits to avoid single tenants hogging.

maya (oncall): starting step 1 now — enabling model-fallback policy to route new requests over 512 tokens to `redwood/gpt-3l-quant-fast` when primary is saturated.

infra-bot: action: routing policy change applied to route-rule id=route-549 to variant=gpt-3l-quant-fast.

sroder: step 2 — canceling queued low-priority jobs. Running: ```redis-cli -h queue-host LRANGE hosted-high 0 -1``` then filter by priority flag. I'll push cancel script.

lucas: I can also flip autoscaler to use warm-spares in other region as fallback. but cross-region introduces latency for some customers. propose: enable cross-region routing only for non-SLA tenants.

nina-prodops: agree. enact cross-region for non-enterprise tiers only. maya, can you apply routing policy?

maya (oncall): applying now. command: `redctl routes set --selector tier!=enterprise --fallback-region us-east-1`. Doing it.

deploy-bot: notice: route config update deployed (id: r-20260314-77).

helen-support: informing affected customers: posting to status page and sending batch emails to high-traffic tenants. Draft message ready: "We're seeing degraded latency for hosted API due to a regional GPU capacity issue; we're routing non-enterprise traffic to alternate regions and enabling model fallbacks. Enterprise customers on Dedicated unaffected if they had failover configured." Approve?

nina-prodops: send it. include ETA: 60-90m for mitigation to reduce error rate.

sroder: temporary knob: reduce max-generation-length default for public keys to 256 tokens, reduces steady-state GPU load. maya: can you flip the global param?

maya (oncall): doing `cfg set default_max_tokens 256 --scope=public`. applied.

lucas: autoscaler side note — cloud provider showing API 429s on instance create. we should switch to shorter, more frequent instance requests and prefer smaller instance types (4x A10 instead of single 8x). but that requires rebalancing pool. I'm starting a script to prefer smaller instances.

sroder: good — start it but keep monitoring memory footprint. small instance packing might impact per-request latency.

incident-bot: update: incident created INC-2026-0314-051. Severity: SEV2. ETA for next update: 15m.

helen-support: logged to status: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-0314-051 — customers notified.

nina-prodops: tracking list: throttled tenants, routed-to-quant, default_max_tokens reduced, queued-batches canceled, cross-region for non-enterprise. Any tasks to hand over to next oncall?

maya (oncall): yes — I'll hand off at +1h. need someone to continue: monitor p99, confirm autoscaler retries stop returning QuotaExceeded, watch error rate drop under 1%. Also escalate to cloud-accounts if quota doesn't free.

sroder: leaving notes: run `aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-12345 --desired-value 64` and attach INC-2026-0314-051. I've already placed request but likely manual review.

lucas: temporary safety valve — enable degraded-mode that serves from LRU cache for repeat prefixes. It's low quality but prevents 504 flood. enabling now.

maya (oncall): degraded-mode on. config id dm-499 applied. p99 dropped to ~7s in a few minutes. queue depth 18k -> 5.2k.

helen-support: customers reporting improvements. some still seeing ~6-8s but fewer timeouts. We should update customers with ETA reduction.

nina-prodops: next steps for postmortem: timelines of autoscaler failures, quota root cause, why warm-spare capacity wasn't used earlier, and validate runbooks for cross-region routing. Assigning owners: sroder for autoscaler logs, lucas for cloud-account escalation, maya for runbook and handoff.

maya (oncall): handing off to lucas for next 2h. lucas, you're oncall takeover. my shift ends in 20m.

lucas: taking over. monitoring dashboards and cloud quota queue. I'll escalate to cloud-accounts if quota doesn't resolve.

incident-bot: handoff recorded: previous_oncall=maya, new_oncall=lucas. next_update_due=1787659025.

helen-support: continuing customer comms. will mark enterprise tenants that still require manual failover.

nina-prodops: closing log: baseline mitigations applied. leaving this thread — will join postmortem sync.

lucas: note for handoff later: confirm autoscaler can pick up smaller instance types and that routing rollback key is `route-549`. Also check metrics for model-fallback error budgets.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: p99 ~6.9s, error rate 0.9%, queue depth 4,900. Severity lowered to SEV3. monitoring continues.

maya (oncall): thanks team. heading out.

lucas: will keep thread updated with any new quota failures or customer escalations.

helen-support: thanks all, will append customer notes and close tickets if stable.
